updates.how: A new floor board has been designed in conjunction with floor edge and diffuser, aiming at improved flow conditioning and aerodynamic load.
A small modification to the rear floor furniture, manipulating rear corner and diffuser flow with the aim of increasing aerodynamic efficiency.

updates.change: Various winglet devices removed from rear wing
updates.how: Removing the rear wing winglets reduces assembly camber shedding local downforce and drag at a ratio appropriate for Vegas L/D.
The mirror stay trim reduces local camber and loading, shedding local downforce and drag at a ratio appropriate for Vegas L/D.

updates.change: Rear corner winglets position and span
updates.how: Rear corner winglets position and span optimised around local load requirements, shedding local downforce and drag at a ratio appropriate for Vegas L/D.
A narrower rear exit allows more cooling range, appropriate for the lower cooling requirements of Vegas.
In order to better protect the flow stability of the front wing endplate footplate as well as surfaces downstream, the dive-plane has been lowered and reduced in chord length.

updates.change: Front floor board elements optimisation, single vertical element
updates.how: The primary aim of these modifications has been to adapt to Las Vegas circuit peculiar characteristics and car aerodynamic efficiency requirements. It is targeting aerodynamic drag saving, coming along with downforce reduction as a natural consequence, but in a favourable ratio for this track.
A reduction in the amount of load generated by the Floor Board provides an improvement in overall efficiency and lap time around this circuit.
An alternative winglet arrangement on the rear brake drums delivers an efficient load reduction, providing a net performance benefit at this track.
A low-balance front wing flap, featuring chord and incidence changes, is available for this circuit to reduce the load generated by the front wing and extend the available balance range.

updates.change: Revised rear wing arrangement associated with the Straight Mode mechanism
updates.how: The revised arrangement is intended to evaluate an alternative rear wing Straight Mode deployment, with associated minor changes to accommodate the different configuration.
The revised rear brake duct deflector geometry was modified to match the specific aerodynamic efficiency requirements of the Las Vegas track.
